image.alt: A massive cloud of white vapor billows out from a structure where an RS-25 engine is firing. The flames are just barely visible through the structure. In the foreground is a body of water.

title: NASA conducts hot fire test of RS-25 engine at Stennis Space Center
excerpt: The test of engine No. 10001 lasted 500 seconds at a 111% power level.
bodyHtml:
NASA teams at Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, conducted a hot fire test of RS-25 engine No. 10001 on October 21, 2026. The test lasted for 500 seconds, which is the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during the launch of the Space Launch System rocket.

The engine operated at a 111% power level during the test. NASA and its prime engine contractor, L3Harris Technologies, will use the data captured from this developmental engine to improve engine performance and reliability.

Prior to use, all RS-25 engines are proven flightworthy at NASA Stennis. For each Artemis mission, four RS-25 engines produce up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust to help launch the Space Launch System rocket.
